lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice distinguishing plans with ska from neutral expectations with kommer att.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Two colleagues talk about the rest of the day and what they expect will happen later.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Talking about plans and likely future events.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik discuss after-work plans, the weather, and what they think will happen during the evening.

main_focus.name: ska versus kommer att
main_focus.description: Use ska for intentions or arranged plans and kommer att for expectations or predictions.
model_examples: Jag ska träffa en vän efter jobbet.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use ska and kommer att naturally 2-3 times each in the dialogue.

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use concrete everyday plans and simple predictions.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person asks about plans for later.
dialogue_shape.middle: They contrast intended actions with expected weather or timing.
dialogue_shape.ending: They settle on what will probably happen.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat both future forms in clearly different contexts

focus: the future event or condition that is only expected
how the expectation affects the plan

sentence_focus: one sentence with ska for a plan
one sentence with kommer att for a prediction
one question asking about later plans
one sentence with jag tror att plus future meaning
one sentence connecting a plan to expected weather or timing
